description:
A field access on a receiver settled as `resource(T)` is currently analyzed as though it were only a map lookup. `LoweredStep::FieldAccess` calls `Types::map_field_lookup`; because a resource has no map axis, `None` is widened to `any`.

This loses two facts:

1. `resource(T).value` is the language-defined payload projection and should type as `T`.
2. Any other named field on a definitely-resource receiver is impossible and should be rejected before backend execution.

Repro:

```fz
defmodule R do
  @type t :: opaque resource(integer)
  fn unwrap(h), do: h.value
  fn bad(h), do: h.foo
end

extern "C" fn fz_resource_test_print_dtor(integer) :: nil
fn dwrap(x), do: fz_resource_test_print_dtor(x)

fn main() do
  a = make_resource(10, &dwrap/1)
  dbg(R.unwrap(a))
  dbg(R.bad(a))
end
```

At `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, the semantic dump reports both `R.unwrap/1[resource(a0_p)] => any` and `R.bad/1[resource(a0_p)] => any`. Interp reaches runtime and exits 1; JIT and the built AOT binary abort the host process at `runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1654`.

Root:

- `src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs:504-512` applies map-only field lookup and widens failure to `any`.
- `Types::resource_payload_type` already provides the resource payload projection.
- Exact access spans are discarded during body lowering: neither `ExprStep::FieldAccess` nor `LoweredStep::FieldAccess` carries a `Span`.

Strategy:

- Preserve the source span of expression field accesses through body lowering into semantic analysis.
- Classify field access using the settled receiver domain:
  - for a definitely-resource receiver and field `value`, use `resource_payload_type`, subject to the existing opaque-ownership visibility contract;
  - for a definitely-resource receiver and any other field, emit one stable diagnostic at the access span;
  - retain conservative `any` only where the receiver domain genuinely remains capable of an unknown map/struct field.
- Keep the runtime `expect` as an unreachable compiler-invariant guard.

Acceptance:

- The negative repro is rejected during compilation by interp, run, and build with the same stable diagnostic code and the precise `h.foo` span.
- Semantic type evidence shows `R.unwrap/1[resource(integer)] => integer`, not `any`.
- `R.unwrap(a)` continues to print `10` on interp, JIT, and AOT.
- Add focused coverage distinguishing definite resource fields from genuinely unknown/dynamic map or struct access.
- Keep `matrix::resource_lifecycle`, `matrix::file_handle`, `matrix::file_resource_lifecycle`, and `matrix::a-resource_aot_dtor` green, followed by full lib and fixture-matrix verification.
title: [BUG] Diagnose impossible resource fields and type .value as the resource payload
